A branch is a region. Its inputs need no ports. Its outputs are joins.

Update, 2026-09-02 08:47. You read this and picked V1: wires always, no ports on the region, exclusivity carried by the wires and read through two views. The hinge below fired exactly as written ("a container has no ports" is a gate). §0 prototypes what you asked for; its second pass (09:30) folds your six points in: transparency is the branch's only control, Case view is Expanded with one arm open, a make-active target on every header, the condition on the band, folding to the header; the third (10:51) drops the one-of sub-slots for one plain port with ordinary fan-in, and Case view now draws only the open case's wires. The rest of the page is unchanged as the record of how the pick was made.

You asked whether an if is a block or a region, whether cables may wire straight to the calls inside, and whether the arms may recombine afterwards. The prior art (LabVIEW, Simulink, MLIR, the sea-of-nodes IR, the program dependence graph) agrees with your instinct on the first two and answers the third with one idea: the merge is a real thing in the program, a φ, and it lives on the region's exit. Five boards below make that judgeable; the recommendation is V2, with V1 as the gesture that authors it.

0 · Your pick, prototyped (second pass): fold, active, one open at a time

Your six points on the first pass are the model here. Transparency is the only thing a branch controls: hide and tunnel are gone from the branch (per-edge Tunnel already exists in pyblocks and stays a property of the edge). Case view is the Expanded layout with at most one arm open, every arm header still visible, no ◀ ▶. Every arm header carries a make-active target; clicking the active one again clears it, and no active arm means all arms are active. The value that decides the branch lands on the band, never on an arm. A folded arm keeps only its header, and in Expanded view its cables attach at the row's edge centres, the way Simple view attaches cables to a Block; in Case view the folded arms' wires are not drawn at all. The consumer has one plain port: the arms' cables fan into encode.pose the way any fan-in does, with no sub-slots.

What the second pass settles (third pass, 10:51: single port, Case view hides folded wires). (1) Fold and active are orthogonal and both survive the view switch: Case view adds the one-open rule and drops the wires of every folded arm, so the open case reads as one straight dataflow. (2) Folding composes with nesting: fold the outer safe arm and the inner region folds with it, its cables collapsing onto the outer header; open safe and fold only (unchanged) and the pass-through becomes a cable into that header and a cable out of it. (3) Because the condition lives on the band, an arm header has exactly two affordances, fold and make-active, and nothing else to learn. (4) The per-edge Tunnel (tunnelRouteIsRevealed in pyblocks: the long run hides, the two stubs stay, revealed by its layer, the edge, an endpoint node, or a port reattachment) is the right tool for one noisy cable; the branch never needs it.

1 · Your thinking, sharpened

Region, not block: agreed, and it is not a taste call. Every representation that has to be correct rather than pretty already does this. The program dependence graph makes an if a control-dependence region whose children are the statements it governs [23]; the sea-of-nodes IR has a Region node with φ nodes hanging off it [20]; MLIR's scf.if is an operation with two regions and a yield [24]; LabVIEW's Case Structure is a region on the diagram [1]. Two ecosystems that began with switch/merge token routing, TensorFlow and V8, moved to the region form [27][22]. None of them makes the branch a callable with a signature, because it has none. Definitions are reused; branches are not, which is exactly your "branches are not like defs" line.

The asymmetry that resolves "fake ports". LabVIEW gives its region tunnels on both sides. MLIR gives its region tunnels on only one: "operations inside a region can reference values defined outside of the region", so there are no input tunnels, but "a value defined in a region can never be used outside of the region": every result leaves through scf.yield, and both arms must yield the same number and types [24][25]. Every system that lets a value be defined on both arms and used after has exactly one join construct per leaving value: Dennis's merge, the φ, the Merge block, the output tunnel [15][19][29][3]. That asymmetry is the whole design. Input tunnels are fake because they only restate visibility; the binding table below shows every arm input resolving to something defined before the region. Output tunnels are not fake, because the name after the if is a genuine join: pose means "whichever arm ran". In SSA that join is a φ. Your "fake ports" reaction is correct about inputs and wrong about outputs, and V2 is what you get when you keep exactly the real half.

LabVIEW could not show both arms because of tunnels, which is the strongest argument for dropping them. NI's help is definitive that only one case of a Case Structure is visible at a time [1][2], and the Idea Exchange request to show a True/False structure's two cases stacked was declined by NI staff with two reasons: "I don't like the wires that point nowhere. Imagine you have 20 cases!", and that the LEGO Mindstorms NXT editor, which does stack its cases, "works because there's almost always only one wire" and becomes "a pain to work with when you start adding additional tunnels" [5]. Green and Petre's cognitive-dimensions study measured the cost of the "invisible arms": every subject did worse on LabVIEW conditionals than on text [6]. Those objections are objections to tunnels, not to side-by-side arms. A cable that runs to a real inner port points somewhere; there is nothing to duplicate per case. Your "wire directly to the functions inside" is what makes side-by-side arms viable at all.

The one shipped precedent is Blender's zones, and it has exactly this asymmetry. Across eighteen node editors, none draws a conditional as a region without border ports. But Blender's Repeat, Simulation and Closure zones are semantic regions whose input side is portless: "nodes inside the zone can also take inputs from nodes outside the zone… however, nodes inside the zone can't send their outputs to nodes outside the zone", and everything leaves through the zone's Output node [46][47][48]. That is scopes-see-in, yields-come-out, shipped for loops. Blender never built a conditional zone, so its if stays a Switch node; the region grammar here fills that gap rather than contradicting anything Blender learned.

A select node's laziness is a property of the engine, not the node, which is why V4 cannot carry a statement. The same "Switch" is lazy in Blender, Houdini SOPs, Nuke and TouchDesigner because those graphs pull, and evaluates both sides in Unreal's Select, Unity's Shader Graph, Grasshopper and Dynamo because those push [42][49][51][57][59][69][71]. Houdini ships both behaviours under one name (the VOP Switch says "all inputs are evaluated"). A board that means "only one of these calls runs" cannot delegate that meaning to whichever runtime happens to read it; the region says it structurally.

Arm order is a layout law, not a preference. DRAKON's rules for exactly this problem: the main route lies on the skewer, "the further to the right, the worse", and no line may cross [81]. Read top-to-bottom instead of left-to-right, that is: arms in source order, the happy path first, and cables that enter an arm only from the shared area to its left.

"Cables cannot cross rows" is derived, not styled. Your Aug 27 red circle (a cable from the if arm dropping into the else arm) is not a layout rule to enforce; it is unrepresentable. An arm starts from a copy of the binding table as it was before the region, so a name read inside the else arm can only resolve to something defined before the region or inside the else arm itself. The probe below runs that lowering over the 09 golden and a nested elif and counts sibling-arm reads: zero. The green circle (a cable entering the else arm from the shared area on the left) is the only other kind there is.

No parallel universes, because the board is the program, not a trace. The "future paths" drawing (two encode()s) is a trace tree: it draws every execution rather than the one text. A CFG draws the text once and lets a path be selected; the φ's definition is exactly that "each execution of a φ-function uses only one of the operands" [19]. That reconciles your two instincts: draw one static board, and make "highlight only certain branches" a lens over it (fixture D). Same call count as the code, always.

Conditional returns are already solved, and they are the next golden. "Different returns represent different output rows" is the half-line output group you ratified on Aug 25 and shipped as branchStart. Inside the expanded def, each return cables to its own boundary output row; the caller sees the split port. Nothing new is needed except the analyzer producing the rows from return sites, and the ladder's case 13 (early return / multiple exits) is precisely that fixture. Forbidding it would forbid return None guards, so don't.

Fold is the one place computed tunnels come back, and that answers "how do you find the names". Always-expanded is right: a branch has no port view because it has no signature. But if an arm folds, the cables into its blocks need somewhere to land, and that somewhere is a tunnel: one stub per distinct incoming cable, named by the inner port it was headed for, ordered by the inner block's position. The names are read off the cables, never authored. Fold reintroduces LabVIEW's tunnels for exactly as long as the arm is folded, and only on that arm.

LabVIEW's unwired-tunnel error is Python's may-be-unbound. In G, an output tunnel that some case leaves unwired is a broken wire unless you tick "Use Default If Unwired", which the style guides warn against because a silent default hides a missing case [3][11]. In Python, pose written only in the if arm and read after the region raises UnboundLocalError on the other path. The probe marks that φ arm UNBOUND; V2 draws it as a hollow red yield (fixture E). That is a diagnostic the collapsed-region lowering cannot express today.

2 · What the tree does today, measured

The analyzer's _lower_region collapses every if into one opaque node and recovers its boundary from a read/write sweep. On the 09 golden that gives the region 5 inputs (estimate, fallback, fast, frame, gain) and 1 output (pose after), with the diagnostic "branch bodies are collapsed; inputs/possible outputs are recovered without choosing a path". The two calls inside the arms are not blocks; they arrive as free values. This is the "port view with named ports" you rejected, generated automatically.

def run(raw: bytes, gain: float, fast: bool) -> bytes:
    frame = decode(raw)
    if fast:
        pose = estimate(frame, gain)
    else:
        pose = fallback(frame)
    payload = encode(pose)
    return payload

The grammar hooks the boards rely on exist in the live block model (read from src/blocks/blockModel.ts and src/blocks/connections/ConnectionShapeUtil.tsx at build time):

  • groupStart — Begins a new async body row; ignored on a side's first port.
  • branchStart — Outputs only: begins a conditional branch within the current row.
  • header — Inputs only: place the port's dot in the heading band.
  • expandedWeights — Manual expanded-section weights keyed by `g:<id>` / `b:<id>`.
  • fanIn — Sources fan out and sinks fan in: a second cable onto an occupied input

Three research passes (LabVIEW from NI's own documentation; dataflow theory and compiler IRs from the papers; a survey of eighteen node editors from their manuals). Cited inline by source number; the index is at the end. The survey's headline: no tool draws a conditional as a region without border ports, and the nearest thing, Blender's zones, keeps the output tunnel and drops the input one.

5 · Criteria, then five boards

  • c1 · Dataflow evident at the join (25) — Tracing a downstream port backwards, the reader sees exactly-one-of without a legend. Zach's stated top rule.
  • c2 · Says what the code says (20) — One block per call, the structure of the AST, no parallel universes. Authoring the board is editing the code.
  • c3 · Scales (20) — N consumers of the merged name, a return straight after the if, elif chains, a nested if, a pass-through arm.
  • c4 · Derivable, diagnostic has a home (15) — Every mark comes from the binding table; the may-be-unbound case has a place to be red.
  • c5 · Reuses the settled grammar (10) — Edge-to-edge rows, dividing lines, half lines, header dots, the expanded frame. No new vocabulary to teach.
  • c6 · Buildable on stock tldraw (10) — Frame, children, boundary port, fan-in, binding. No engine fork.

Hinge. V2's only weak criterion is c5, because the region gains a port. If "a container has no ports" is a hard gate rather than a reaction to input tunnels, V2 is out and V1 wins at 78.0. But V1 authored on the canvas is V2's input: two cables from sibling arms landing on one port are the app's cue to derive a yield. And V5 is V2 with the border hidden, which can be an appearance toggle rather than a variant.

V1 · Fan-in at the consumer

78.0/100c1 4 · c2 5 · c3 2 · c4 4 · c5 4 · c6 5

The region has no ports at all. Each arm's producer cables straight to the downstream input, which grows a one-of receiver: two sub-slots and a half line between them, the output-side half-line grammar mirrored onto an input.

best when

One consumer, shallow nesting, and when the board must look exactly like the code's cables.

loses when

N consumers of the merged name cost 2N cables; a return straight after the if lands the fan-in on the frame's boundary output; the reader must inspect a port to learn that only one cable is live.

what exists today

Fan-in onto an input is already legal on the canvas (rule below). What is missing is the one-of mark and the analyzer lowering the arms.

V2 · Yield on the region border

90.0/100c1 5 · c2 4 · c3 5 · c4 5 · c5 3 · c6 4

Inputs need no tunnels because an arm can see everything defined before the region. Outputs are different: every name any arm writes is a real join, so it gets one yield dot on the region's right edge, cabled from each arm, and downstream reads one cable.

best when

Everything the ladder has coming: N consumers, return-after-if, elif chains, nested regions, pass-through arms, and the unbound diagnostic (a hollow yield).

loses when

The region gains a port. If 'a container has no ports' is a hard rule rather than a reaction to input tunnels, this is gated out and V1 is the fallback.

what exists today

The expanded frame already draws boundary ports on its edge with inner faces; a yield is that port with a computed name. The grammar hooks exist: groupStart, branchStart, header.

V3 · Merge node after the region

74.0/100c1 4 · c2 3 · c3 4 · c4 4 · c5 3 · c6 4

Simulink's answer: the region is a bare container and the join is a free-standing φ node placed in the flow, movable like any block. The same node would later carry a loop's back-edge.

best when

When the merge deserves to be a first-class thing you can name, move, and comment.

loses when

It adds a node the code does not have, floats away from the region that owns it, and doubles the node count of every branch.

what exists today

A Block with two inputs and one output is all it is; nothing new in the renderer, one new node kind in the analyzer.

V4 · Select block, no region

54.0/100c1 3 · c2 1 · c3 2 · c4 3 · c5 4 · c6 5

Blender, Houdini and Grasshopper's answer: no region, both producers in the main flow, and a select block whose header takes the condition. Pure dataflow.

best when

A conditional expression, `a if c else b`, where both operands are cheap and pure. The analyzer already lowers IfExp as its own region kind.

loses when

For an if statement it says the wrong thing: both calls appear to run. Side effects and cost vanish from the picture.

what exists today

A Block with a header dot and a half line between its inputs; every mark exists today.

V5 · Divider bands, no frame

74.0/100c1 4 · c2 4 · c3 3 · c4 4 · c5 5 · c6 2

The branch is not a container but a thick divider that starts at a fork dot (the condition lands there) and ends at a join dot (the φ). Arms are the bands above and below it. Nesting is a thinner divider. 'It's all just dividing lines' taken literally.

best when

Shallow branches in a wide flow, and readers who want the least chrome on the canvas.

loses when

A band has no left edge, so nothing tells the reader where an arm begins; a band is not a tldraw shape, so there is no drop target or fold handle without an invisible frame, at which point it is V2 with the border hidden.

what exists today

Nothing draws a divider that is not inside a shape; this needs a frame underneath it anyway.

6 · The recommended board under load

7 · The seam

Analyzer contract, in five rules

  1. An if lowers to one region with N arms: the if, every elif in the chain, and the else. A single If in an orelse is an elif, not a nested region. match is the same shape with a subject on the header.
  2. Each arm is lowered with a copy of the binding table; its calls are ordinary blocks parented to the arm; its reads resolve to outside values or its own definitions. No arm sees a sibling.
  3. Every name written by any arm becomes one yield on the region, with one producer per arm: the arm's last write, a pass-through of the outer value, or UNBOUND (a warning diagnostic). The table after the region maps the name to the yield.
  4. Header reads are the condition's names. They cable to the arm's label-row dot, thick, as your Aug 27 sketch already draws callables and conditions.
  5. A conditional expression (a if c else b) is V4, a select block, because both operands are expressions in one statement; a statement-level if never is.

8 · Decision surface

Done and proved

  • Per-arm binding lowering written and run over the 09 golden and three fixtures: 0 sibling-arm reads, φ per written name, pass-through and UNBOUND both surface.
  • Five boards on one fixture, drawn in the SystemSketch idiom, plus four load fixtures for the recommended one.
  • Prior art gathered from primary sources and reduced to one table.

Left, and what kind of left

  • Next: implement the arm lowering in analyzer.py (elif = sibling arm, copy the table per arm, header reads = condition names); V1 needs no yield node, only one cable per (arm producer → consumer) pair.
  • Next: a region frame kind in SystemSketch with view: expanded | case, an active-arm state, and the one-of receiver mark on inputs; fold with computed stubs.
  • Blocked on nothing.

Needs you (after the third pass)

  • Expanded keeps a folded arm's wires at its header edge; Case drops them. Default if silent: yes.
  • Two affordances per arm header, fold and make-active, nothing else. Default if silent: yes.
  • Fade level for the non-active arms: 18% here. Default if silent: 18%, one token in the theme.
  • Does a folded header show a count (blocks, cables) or stay bare like Simple view? Default if silent: bare.
  • Case view remembers which arm is open per region across reloads. Default if silent: yes, like collapsed state.

Deliberately not done

  • No analyzer or renderer code changed; boards are drawn marks, not live shapes, and say so.
  • No golden target rewritten; the bootstrap's --force rewrites all twelve.
  • No loop design; the same region idiom applies and a back-edge is the next question, not this one.
